title: Leaf-size regularisation reduces measured leakage under a recalibrated attack, with utility reported

invariants.description: Against the regularised forest, the RECALIBRATED threshold attack's AUC must be ≤ 0.65 (observed 0.568, from 0.896 undefended; 20-seed max 0.617).
The shadow attack retrained with the defended recipe must reach AUC ≤ 0.65 (observed 0.539; 20-seed max 0.604).
Correct membership decisions on the SAME 500 candidates must fall significantly (one-sided paired McNemar; observed p ≈ 2e-43; significant on 20/20 seeds).
The defended model's train−test gap must be ≤ 0.15 (observed 0.085; 20-seed range 0.040–0.113).
Held-out accuracy must stay ≥ 0.67 (observed 0.703 vs 0.725 undefended; 20-seed utility drop −0.028 to +0.022).
Regularisation is not a guarantee: a residual signal remains (observed AUC 0.568, threshold leakage still claimed at p = 0.0045; leakage still claimed on 17/20 seeds).

rationale: With at least 25 records per leaf no prediction is determined by one training record, so the confidence gap between members and non-members shrinks. The attacker re-trains its reference and shadow models with the defended recipe (it knows the training procedure); the reduction is measured on the same candidates and comes at little utility cost — but it reduces, it does not remove, leakage.
